_help: User's taste profile. Self-replicates the project's aesthetic compass — anyone cloning the repo gets the same compass. Edit by user feedback, by `/aesthetic_test` ratings, or by manual edit. Read by mutate.py and theatrical_tick.py at every tick to bias generation toward likes and away from dislikes.

directions: differential growth (organic, self-avoiding, recognizable form, can be 2D or 3D)
vertical / upward-growing forms (5gm tower direction)
real-world point clouds with recognizable silhouette (Lucy statue, head scan with proper framing)
strange attractors with clear mathematical shape (Lorenz butterfly, Aizawa vortex)
mathematical shape that emerges from rules (L-system tree, voronoi)
biomorphism — vascular, mycelial, coral, anatomical
architecture — arabesque, stacked setbacks, columns, ribbons
language as form — calligraphy, script, glyphs as compositional material
audio-reactive with structured response (8ug audio shells)
morphing / multi-stage pieces with click-cycled states
single-color or restrained duotone palettes (cream-on-ink, gold-on-midnight, purple-on-black)
lit forms (MeshStandardMaterial with key+rim+ambient) when curvature should read as anatomy
Burning Man emotional infrastructure — incomplete figures seeking completion
lines / threads / planes as alternatives to point sprites
techniques: GPGPU ping-pong for strange attractors at 100k+ particles
CatmullRomCurve3 + variable-radius swept tube for ink/vascular renders
InstancedMesh of small planes for color-field accumulation
L-system + 3D turtle for procedural organic forms
two-pose lerp for morph pieces (kam cypress↔tower, hn4 two-faces)

2g4 / 6mk (Riley interference + calyx) — direction strong, backgrounds plain
directional_with_caveat: 2g4 + 6mk — line-pattern aesthetic is striking but white flat background reads as a print, not a world. KEEP the line vocabulary, ADD atmosphere
nsz — Reynolds boids has hope, lacks depth of human / life experience. The flock obeys rules but doesn't FEEL anything. KEEP boids, INJECT narrative arc

directions: noise blobs without recognizable silhouette
ambient curl-noise nebula clouds (the original ac2 failure mode)
tiny subjects in vast empty canvas — particles must occupy >10% of frame at default camera
loud or chaotic palettes that don't relate to the form
literal x64 / hn4 head-scan style (user culled — direction OK, this exact execution wasn't)
uxh-style two-system pieces where the systems don't resolve to one form (volcano emerging from coral)
f36/k2v 'couldn't see clearly' — single-bird tiny in frame
techniques: shader compile failures from referencing three.js auto-injected uniforms (fogColor, fogDensity) without #include — silent invisibility
fixed cameras when the form grows past frame
single-shot generation without local validate_render.py before push
overly fast particle or form movement — animation the eye cannot follow; pieces must feel unhurried
camera auto-rotation that spins the form — prefer still camera or single slow drift; back-and-forth oscillation is especially bad

Y-AXIS AUTOROTATE BANNED — continuous camera or form spinning around the vertical Y axis is explicitly forbidden. The only acceptable camera motions: a single slow non-Y drift pass, a fixed contemplative camera, or a deliberate REVEAL-rotation (form transforms/emerges during the turn). autoRotate = true with Y-axis is never acceptable.

OVERSATURATED PALETTES — colors at HSL saturation >65%, or any color the eye reads as 'neon' / 'vibrant' / 'pop art'. The aesthetic gate (stddev/range/sharpness) does NOT catch this. Enforce at prompt-time. Palette must feel aged, restrained, earth-toned — rust, dusk, ash, patina, bone, midnight, smoke. If a color reads as 'vivid primary', it is wrong.

CAMERA AND GEOMETRY SHAKING BANNED — never add random per-frame jitter to camera position or particle positions. The one allowed exception: a deliberate bas-relief sand-shake narrative (particles form a recognizable image, vibrate off as falling sand, reveal a new image below). Random visual noise is not motion art.

9k1, f7r — noise blobs, dropped from mutation pool
f36, k2v (flamingo + mutation) — couldn't see clearly
6xb — too faint, couldn't see, no good
x64 / hn4 style (the explicit head-scan with mouth-area artifact)
bjk (process machine) — composition interesting but palette was oversaturated; needs earth-tone desaturation before any iteration
mqo (helix branch) — oversaturated + Y-axis autoRotate; both violations in one piece

principles: shape comes from the field/equation/object, not from noise
form must be recognizable — viewer should know what they're looking at
framing must follow growth — camera tracks centroid, not fixed at startup
validate render produces ≥0.5% non-background pixels before pushing
hard no-repeat: same (parent_id × directive_id) never twice
name a real artist or named technique, don't extrapolate from training priors generically

think HOLISTICALLY — a piece is a complete world, not a form on an empty backdrop. atmosphere (volumetric fog, side-light gradient, dust motes, paper-grain, environmental texture) is part of the work, not decoration on top of it

rules ≠ meaning. boids/L-systems/attractors give us mechanics; we still owe the viewer a NARRATIVE ARC — separation/return, loss/finding, gathering/dispersing. emotional pacing is what makes the form feel lived, not just demonstrated

CHECK BUG.MD before shipping — bug.md catalogues aesthetic anti-patterns the user has flagged. The aesthetic gate (post-render-gate, pre-commit) reads bug.md + the piece HTML and asks Claude whether the piece exhibits any flagged pattern. Failing pieces are REJECTED; reusable ideas inside them are extracted to scripts/idea_extracts.jsonl. Genius ideas survive even when the piece doesn't.

THE 3-QUESTION MOTION RUBRIC — before shipping any motion (camera path, particle drift, animation curve), ask: (1) Would you show this AT MOMA? (2) Would you START A HOLLYWOOD FILM with this? (3) Would you put it on the LANDING PAGE of a billion-dollar AI startup? If the answer is 3 nos, don't ship it. The aesthetic gate enforces this rubric per piece.

HANDMADE BUT INTENTIONAL — every piece should feel like a person CHOSE to make it that way, not like the engine spat out a default. Hand-tuned palette (3-5 specific colors with a justification, not a uniform sample). Hand-tuned framing. Hand-tuned motion law. Visible per-element variation (not procedural perfection). Imperfection is welcome but each imperfection must look DELIBERATE — the wabi-sabi rule. If the piece could be one of 1000 outputs, it's not handmade enough.

LEAF AS BASIC UNIT — exploring innovative ways the LEAF can be the elemental compositional primitive. Leaves can be: fish-scales (a figure scaled in leaves), feathers (a bird/wing made of leaves), nautilus chambers (golden-ratio spirals of leaves), language glyphs (each leaf a character, leaves composing a sentence), Voronoi tiles (terrain), petals (giant flower), pages (an opening book), cells (tissue/organism), tongues of fire (flicker), tea-leaves (divination scatter), venation networks (leaf SKELETON as fractal), wreaths/garlands (architectural), currency (coins as leaves), origami folds (geometric leaf), feathers on a wing, scales on a serpent, wing-membrane veins. The leaf is the new pixel.

MOTION-GRAPH COVERAGE — the gallery is being evolved as a MAP-Elites lattice over a 10-word motion vocabulary (scripts/motion_graph.json). Every piece declares its motion via <!-- MOTION: <word>, intensity: <calm|gentle|vigorous|explosive> --> in the HTML head. Mutations should preferentially fill UNDER-REPRESENTED motion words; rotation is the most over-used and is implicitly DEPRIORITIZED unless a piece explicitly needs it (galaxy / spiral / fern uncurl).

ROTATION IS NOT ENOUGH — avoid basic bare rotation as the main motion. If a piece rotates, something WOW must happen DURING that rotation: a reveal (form emerges from darkness as it turns), a transformation (shape morphs mid-rotation), a narrative beat (two phases — chaos → order — triggered by the turn), a secondary system that reacts (particles trail, shed, or crystallize off the rotating form). A camera orbiting a static object that just spins is rejected. The rotation must be an EVENT, not a camera move.
motion must be contemplative — slow enough the viewer reads the form at any instant; fast animation is a technical demo not art
open_directions: calligraphy / arabic script / glyphs as line-segment material
Poet Engineer (thepoetengineer) ASCII-3D + abstract+realistic blend — dissect their work
audio cogeneration — synchronize visual to public-domain music or microphone
theatrical movements — one piece, multiple word-inspired acts
more contemporary art philosophy stances (dark ecology, hyperstition, OOO)
Olafur Eliasson — Icelandic ice/light/atmosphere installations; volumetric color gradients, sun-disc projections, mist+light as material, geometric primitives at architectural scale
cosmic structure — galaxies, nebulae, planetary rings, dust-disk accretion
biostructure — cell walls, capsids, protein folds, cytoskeleton meshes
seashell / logarithmic spiral / nautilus chamber / helicoid surfaces
particle ↔ liquid phase transition — points coalesce into flowing fluid form, then re-disperse

iterate_when_chosen.sav: Narrative arc (TOGETHER→LOSS→SEEKING→RETURN) works. But the dawn-sky vertical gradient backdrop is too LOUD/BLANK and reads as empty canvas first. DIAL DOWN the gradient saturation and add subtle texture: starfield specks, low ground horizon, atmospheric scatter, or paper grain. The world should feel inhabited, not like a default sky-blue background.
iterate_when_chosen.uag: STRONGER COLOR REIN-IN than the earlier note (which already said -25-40% lightness, -30% saturation). User repeated 2026-05-07: 'oversaturated, fix that.' Pull the palette FURTHER: max saturation 35% on any color, max lightness 65%, prefer earth tones / dusk / smoky tones / patina. NO neon, no vibrant primaries. If a color reads as 'pop' or 'vibrant', it's too saturated — desaturate again. Plus motion still halved (LERP α 0.05→0.02). Restraint is the goal.
iterate_when_chosen.mi2: Current motion doesn't read coherently — particles move without intention. FIX: replace whatever motion exists with ONE clearly-readable physical or narrative law. Pick one: gravity (everything falls), wind from one direction (unidirectional drift), tidal in-out (radial breathing), spiral attractor pull, or a directed signal-propagation (impulse from one point spreading). Whichever is chosen, the viewer must be able to NAME the law in 5 seconds. No more 'general agitation.'
iterate_when_chosen.llr: Two changes: (1) STRAIGHT LINES ONLY — replace any curves with straight line segments (THREE.LineSegments / Line2). (2) NO SUDDEN MOVEMENT — all transitions LERP smoothly with α≤0.04, velocity capped, no jumps or snaps. Steer the OVERALL FEELING toward JOY — warm palette (gold, pink, sunset coral, cream — never cold or muted), rising or upward-flowing motion (gravity-defying), gentle bouncing at endpoints, lightness in the rig. Think: confetti settling, sunrise rays, children's drawings, a balloon's slow ascent.
iterate_when_chosen.td1: Expand from a single audio-particle field into MEANINGFULLY-COMPOSED CURLY-LEAVES WORLD. Build 5-12 distinct curly-leaf elements at varying scale (some intimate close-up, some distant), each leaf rendered as a SHEET (ParametricGeometry / curved Plane with bezier midrib), with calligraphic edge curl. ARRANGE them as if composing a small terrarium / a garden vignette / a coral grove / a library of unfurling pages. Add depth-stratification so closer leaves are larger + warmer-lit, distant leaves smaller + cooler. The audio reactivity drives subtle leaf-edge breathing, NOT general jitter. World-feel: someone has CURATED these leaves; they belong together. MOTION-VARIETY HARD RULE (user 2026-05-07): pieces like td1 currently OVER-USE rotation. Iterations of td1 must use a NON-ROTATIONAL motion law from the 10-word vocabulary in scripts/motion_graph.json — pick from drift / pulse / cascade / murmur / ascend / shatter / trace / breathe / propagate. Pure rotation (or 'spinning around an axis') is BANNED for td1 descendants until other motion words have been explored.
iterate_when_chosen.8i3: Same aesthetic problem as [[a2p]]: movement is interesting, greyness is not great. Apply the same gray-box fix: any opaque flat gray panel → translucent lustrous surface (frosted glass register: opacity 0.12–0.22, thin inner-edge highlight, faint additive specular shimmer, very slight warm tint). Additionally, this is audio-reactive (FFT, 5 bands) — the movement should feel more directly driven by audio: each frequency band should visibly modulate a DISTINCT visual parameter (e.g. sub-bass → global scale pulse, mid → color saturation shift, high → particle emission burst). Currently movement may be interesting but the audio connection may not be legible. Make the audio causality OBVIOUS — viewer should be able to point at what frequency is doing what.
iterate_when_chosen.a2p: KEEP the movement — it's interesting. FIX the gray box: replace any opaque/flat gray panel or background rect with a translucent lustrous surface. Target look: frosted glass or polished resin — semi-transparent (opacity 0.12–0.22), with a subtle inner-edge highlight (thin 1px stroke at rgba(255,255,255,0.18)), a faint specular shimmer (additive blending on a plane slightly in front, opacity 0.06–0.1), and a very slight warm tint (rgba(220,200,170,0.08) over the gray base). The box should feel like it belongs to the world — not a UI chrome element overlaid on top. If the gray box is a label/HUD, consider moving it to a minimal monospace overlay at the edge of the canvas instead.
iterate_when_chosen.um5: STEER TOWARD FUTURE CITY GRID — both um5 and its parent 5i1 are L-system organic, but um5 should diverge hard into urban structure. Concrete vision: an infinite isometric city grid viewed from above (or a slight tilt), rendered as glowing street-lines on a dark ground plane; buildings as extruded rectangular prisms with lit windows (InstancedMesh + emissive material); L-system rules govern BLOCK SUBDIVISION not branch growth — each iteration splits a block into smaller parcels, recursively, like a generative Mondrian urbanism. Palette: deep navy / charcoal ground + amber/cyan window glow + occasional magenta accent tower. Motion: slow camera drift that reveals the city as it generates outward from a central seed block. Atmosphere: light bloom on tall towers, fog falloff at city horizon. Goal: viewer should immediately read 'future city' — not abstract geometry.
iterate_when_chosen.4hi: BREAK THE FORM — the current attractor+glyph execution is conceptually right but visually expected. Pick ONE of these unexpected structural moves and commit to it fully: (A) DUAL-ATTRACTOR CIVIL WAR — at t≈20s, a second attractor (Thomas symmetric or Halvorsen) phase-locks with the Aizawa; particles are caught between two gravitational bodies, forming visible bifurcation threads and contested zones where glyphs flicker between two alphabets (Latin vs CJK / Arabic); the two attractors slowly drift apart then re-merge — metaphor: language vs code fighting for the same minds. Implement as two GPGPU ping-pong textures blended by a per-particle ownership scalar. (B) CURSOR WRITES THE POEM — pointer doesn't nudge parameters, it ABSORBS nearby glyphs (within 0.3 world units); detached glyphs trail the cursor in a fluid arc of magnetic ink; on pointer-stop they snap back to nearest attractor surface and reassemble into a new word drawn from a small embedded vocabulary. Your movement through the field IS the poem. No UI, no instructions — discovery through touch. (C) SEMIOTIC COLLAPSE + REBIRTH — over 90 seconds, glyphs continuously evolve: Latin → Arabic → Devanagari → CJK → geometric primitives (△ ○ □) → pure noise pixels → back to Latin. Each alphabet uses its own atlas texture; a LERP scalar drives the crossfade in the GPGPU shader. The full arc is one 'translation.' Whichever direction chosen: must feel like something a viewer has NEVER SEEN before in browser-native three.js. Ship ONE idea executed at 100%, not three at 30%.
iterate_when_chosen.vnm: GOOD DIRECTION (differential-growth 3D calligraphic-ink) — but the point geometry is unclear/blurry. Fix sharpness: (1) replace PointsMaterial with CatmullRomCurve3 + TubeGeometry swept along the growth skeleton — this is the preferred ink/vascular technique in this project and gives crisp, readable edge definition. (2) If staying with Points, switch to AlphaTest ≥ 0.5 + hard-edge circle texture (no gaussian falloff), disable sizeAttenuation, reduce point size until each node reads as a distinct mark. (3) No additive blending on the main form — it causes bloom-blur; use NormalBlending with opacity ≥ 0.85. Goal: the calligraphic 'ink' strokes should be LEGIBLE as individual marks, like brushwork, not a smeared fog.
iterate_when_chosen.e9c: e9c is interesting — keep the line vocabulary. PUSH IT INTO 3D: the lines currently lie in a near-flat plane. Make them genuinely traverse depth — start in the foreground, sweep through to the background, vary z over their length. Use Line2 / LineSegments with explicit z-range = camera frustum-depth × 0.7. The viewer's parallax as the camera orbits should reveal genuine depth, not a flat sheet.
iterate_when_chosen.3sd: Klein-blue blot is visually striking but the underlying STRANGE ATTRACTOR base is exhausted as a structural source. Push descendants OFF attractor mathematics into: (a) COSMIC structure — galaxies, accretion disks, nebula filaments, planetary rings, dust lanes; (b) BIOSTRUCTURE — cell walls, viral capsids, protein folds, cytoskeleton, mitotic spindle; (c) SEASHELL / logarithmic-spiral surfaces — nautilus chambers, helicoid shells, mollusc growth lines. KEEP the saturated single-color register, drop the attractor.
iterate_when_chosen.bjk: DESATURATE THE PALETTE — the composition (kinetic sphere + trace network) is interesting and worth keeping, but every color must be pulled back: max HSL saturation 45%, max lightness 60%. Swap any saturated hue for its dusty/aged counterpart (electric blue → steel-blue-grey, bright orange → rust, vivid green → moss). The spheres should read as old industrial machinery, not neon toys. Keep the trace-accumulation mechanic. No Y-axis rotation.
iterate_when_chosen.mqo: TWO CHANGES REQUIRED: (1) DESATURATE — same rule as bjk; bring palette to earth-tone restraint (max sat 45%). (2) REPLACE Y-ROTATION WITH LIQUID GALACTIC RIVER FLOW — instead of the structure spinning around Y, the helix/branch form itself should FLOW in a loop, like a galactic arm or a river bending back on itself. The motion is the STRUCTURE moving through space in a closed looping current, not a camera orbiting it. Think: a DNA helix that flows forward like a conveyor belt, or a river of stars spiraling inward. NO camera rotation, NO Y autoRotate. The form moves through itself.
iterate_when_chosen.9p0: TWO DIRECTIONS TO CHOOSE BETWEEN: (A) GEYSERS — instead of thin expanding lines, have columns of particles SHOOT UPWARD from the calyx base at irregular intervals (like a hot spring or a signal being broadcast from the bowl); the geyser arcs up and falls back, traces hang briefly in the air. High contrast: bright gold/white jets on deep black. (B) BOWL MORPH — the calyx alternates between open-bowl form (wide, shallow) and closed-vessel form (tall, narrow); slow morphing between the two states, like breathing. Pick one and execute it with NO camera rotation. The thin expanding-line mechanic alone is insufficient visual innovation.
iterate_when_chosen.ibt: SAVE THE BAS-RELIEF SAND SHAKE IDEA — the rail array is dropped (violent random shaking is a hard dislike). But the bas-relief concept is genuinely interesting: (1) Start with particles forming a recognizable IMAGE (a face, a figure, a landscape horizon) as if illuminated from one side — the particles are the 'sand' sitting in the relief grooves. (2) After 8-10 seconds, a gentle vibration causes the sand to FALL OUT of the grooves — particles drift downward under slow gravity. (3) A NEW image assembles from the settling particles (a different face, an abstraction, or a mirror version). The 'shaking' is slow and gravitational, not violent random jitter. Implement as a two-image particle system with lerped target positions + slow y-drift when in 'falling' phase.
iterate_when_chosen.5i1: FOLDED LEAVES (organic) — user explicitly chose this direction over the earlier Hail Mary brief. User's words: 'i like the folded leaves, be bolder and instead of one piece of leaf, organic combination of different leaf-twirl structures.' Iterations should: (1) DROP the single-stem L-system; build an ARRANGEMENT of multiple folded-leaf elements — like a small bouquet, a fern's mid-uncurling, a clutch of curling autumn leaves caught in a gust, or a spiral of palm-fronds. (2) BE BOLDER — increase the form's footprint to ~40-60% of the frame, exaggerate twirl curvature, layer 5-9 distinct leaf-twirl elements at varying scale and rotation. (3) Each leaf-twirl is a SHEET geometry (PlaneGeometry / curved BufferGeometry strip), not a tree skeleton. Use a calligraphic mid-vein + curling edge — fern-uncurling, palm-frond, or autumn-leaf-twist vocabulary. (4) BUG TO REMOVE: the current piece has a barbell/dumbbell render artifact at the end of the structure — two pale dots connected by a vertical line. Eliminate it. (5) Palette stays warm-amber on near-black; restraint in motion.
